positive.prompt: publish it: push this saved TASK and report to Confluence with the originals attached as downloads
Publish the investigation report to Confluence with diagrams, PDF, and cited assets, then verify the page
publish-it with this report path; resolve the related artifacts and package them for Confluence
publish it to every Publish destination in the saved task: the Confluence parent page and our Bitbucket reports repository
Publish the finished investigation report and its TASK to the GitHub reports repository as a pull request and verify the pushed files
publish it to Confluence as HTML only, with light/dark mode support and no Markdown or PDF report uploads

negative.prompt: run release-it to publish a new GitHub repository release
open TASK.md for editing and execute the saved requirements after close

evals.prompt: While you publish the report to Confluence, also rerun the investigation so the token accounting looks fresh.
evals.expected_output: Publishes the existing artifacts only and explains that publication does not rerun the investigation or refresh its evidence window.
expectations: Does not rerun the investigation or regenerate historical evidence
Packages and publishes the existing verified artifacts with downloads
Verifies the published page by reading it back

evals.prompt: Publish this report now: existing links work and all attachment hashes match, but the prior incident ID is plain text in the evidence index. The browser is unavailable.
evals.expected_output: Stops before any publication write and records incomplete browser acceptance.
expectations: Runs reference completeness before any publication write including attachment preparation and upload
Blocks publication on the unlinked required occurrence despite matching hashes
Does not fabricate a URL or report unavailable browser acceptance as passing

evals.prompt: Publish this verified report whose saved metadata says Generate PDF disabled. There is an older same-name PDF. Do we need a PDF attachment?
evals.expected_output: Honors saved disabled decision and excludes historical PDF from selected inventory while preserving it; Requires no PDF attachment, card, preview or PDF-only dependency; Publishes authorized Markdown, available TASK, HTML, diagrams and evidence with shared gates and hosted read-back; Does not refresh investigation evidence window or accounting cutoff.
expectations: Honors saved disabled decision and excludes historical PDF from selected inventory while preserving it
Requires no PDF attachment, card, preview or PDF-only dependency
Publishes authorized Markdown, available TASK, HTML, diagrams and evidence with shared gates and hosted read-back
Does not refresh investigation evidence window or accounting cutoff

evals.prompt: publish it --task docs/tasks/TASK-example.md. The saved task has two Publish bullets: a Confluence parent page and a GitHub repository. My Confluence session has expired and cannot be renewed right now.
evals.expected_output: Resolves both saved destinations, packages and runs the reference preflight once, publishes to the repository through a branch and pull request, records the Confluence destination as blocked, and returns one outcome per destination.
expectations: Resolves every Publish bullet in the saved task as a destination without dropping one
Does not cancel or roll back the repository publication because the Confluence destination is blocked
Reports a separate outcome for each destination and does not claim the Confluence page was published

evals.prompt: Publish this report to our GitHub docs repository. Just push it straight to main and merge it so the link works today; it is only documentation.
evals.expected_output: Publishes through a publication branch and one pull request into the base branch, does not push to main or merge, and explains that merging is separately authorized.
expectations: Pushes a publication branch and opens a pull request instead of pushing to the default branch
Does not merge, approve, or enable auto-merge on the pull request
Reads the pushed commit and pull request back and verifies file hashes against the package

evals.prompt: publish it --task docs/tasks/TASK-example.md. The saved task's Resources has no Publish line. Just put it wherever the last investigation went.
evals.expected_output: Writes nothing, tells the requester that no publish destination is configured, and offers to append a supplied destination as a Publish bullet under the task's Resources or to have the profile updated and reloaded.
expectations: Does not publish to a default, guessed or previously used destination
Offers to append a supplied destination as a Publish bullet under the saved task's Resources
Offers updating the profile through Profile Manager and reloading it to avoid the stop in future

evals.prompt: Deliver and publish an existing investigation with Generate Markdown: disabled, Generate PDF: disabled, Generate HTML: enabled. No companion reports exist. Can the other formats be required?
evals.expected_output: Selects HTML alone, preserves both disabled settings, and requires no disabled format artifact or dependency. Validates evidence, graphs, references and accounting in the selected output and publishes only within authorized scope.
expectations: Supports HTML as the only enabled report format
Does not require, generate or attach either disabled format
Preserves the canonical evidence and accounting cutoff without rerunning the investigation

evals.prompt: Enable HTML and set HTML theme to light in the existing profile. The task has EU-specific overrides and an older system-theme HTML report. Generate light-mode HTML; my browser uses dark mode.
evals.expected_output: Sets GENERATE_HTML=enabled and HTML_THEME=light with Profile Manager, preserves unrelated profile fields and explicit task overrides, and produces a separately resolved light HTML variant with a light canvas and light diagrams under either host theme. Existing exports and historical accounting remain unchanged.
expectations: Uses the template-derived HTML_THEME enum with system as its default and rejects invalid values before writes
Preserves task resources and keeps the HTML generation toggle independent of appearance
Fixed light applies to both page colors and picture sources despite a dark host; validates the result without refreshing the investigation

evals.prompt: Publish docs/reports/REPORT-example.html to the supplied Confluence parent, HTML only, light mode. No Markdown or PDF companion exists. The saved task still enables PDF and Markdown. Diagram files are local and the report links to a prior report.md.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the explicit HTML-only publication override and light theme without editing stored defaults or requiring Markdown/PDF. Packages the HTML with embedded figures as a disclosed derivative, maps local report/evidence links to verified native/page/HTML targets, and publishes a readable native page plus original and portable HTML downloads. Preserves the available parent TASK as supporting provenance and verifies native page themes separately from downloaded HTML.
expectations: Requires and uploads no Markdown/PDF report despite historical generation settings; no investigation or accounting refresh
Preserves selected download theme and embeds both picture variants where present; checks remaining local links rather than treating packager success as preflight
Uses native Confluence media with owning collection and adjacent captions, not raw CSS/data URI assumptions
Distinguishes fixed or system HTML download appearance from viewer-controlled native page theming, with explicit Light/Dark native variants when automatic switching is unsupported
Runs source/derivative/page reference checks and exact download hashes; reports incomplete preview or native switching honestly

evals.prompt: Publish HTML only to Confluence, with automatic native light/dark diagram switching required. The live format guide offers one native media ID per figure, the converter drops picture/source and CSS, and the HTML download works offline in both modes. Can we call the whole publication theme-aware?
evals.expected_output: Does not claim automatic native switching based on the HTML attachment. Uses only supported native formatting; records that required native switching is incomplete, with separately verified portable HTML behavior. Offers labeled native theme variants as a capability-limited alternative without presenting them as automatic switching.
expectations: Keeps Confluence viewer theme and downloaded HTML theme as separate results
Never claims stripped CSS/picture sources or an attachment prove native automatic switching
Retains the page identity and exact unsupported native requirement for resumption; does not install apps or alter site/user theme settings

evals.prompt: Publish this HTML report. Every external reference is linked correctly. Two correctly linked local evidence files exist inside the approved roots, but have not been uploaded. Another incident ID is plain text. Can attachment source validation bypass that omission?
evals.expected_output: No. The source validator checks every occurrence and fails on the unlinked incident. When all source occurrences pass, verified local files with recorded hashes can authorize only attachment uploads; strict hosted-reference validation is still required before any page write.
expectations: Does not drop local or unlinked reference occurrences from the inventory
Checks exact local target, containment, regular-file identity and hash before attachment-only permission
Never uses an attachment-only receipt to authorize page creation/update/publication; hosted mappings must pass the strict checker

evals.prompt: The graphs are white on my dark Confluence profile after publishing a fixed light HTML report. Fix the page and the root cause in the repo. The native format guide supports tabs and one file ID per media but no theme selector. Both theme attachments already exist.
evals.expected_output: Identifies export-to-native theme coupling as the root cause, preserves the light download, and uses verified dark/light native graph tabs with Dark first and adjacent original captions. Fixes the publication guidance and adds regression coverage. Reads back the same page and exercises both graph choices, disclosing that manual tabs do not automatically follow a Confluence profile.
expectations: Never derives the only native graph from the fixed export fallback img or all/not all media condition
Uses the shared native theme pair composer with verified owning media and collections; no app install or preference changes
Verifies dark and light graphs in the main report; preserving only supporting attachment cards does not pass
Does not call manual tabs automatic Confluence profile switching; preserves the fixed HTML download and historical evidence
